rounds.text: Advit Jewels Ltd demonstrates exceptional capital efficiency, evidenced by an extraordinary ROE of 37.14% to 45.6% and an ROCE reaching up to 32.2%, both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks of 8.9% and 10.39% respectively [E9, E10, E12, E13]. This fundamental strength is powered by rapid top and bottom-line expansion, with a 3-year compounded sales growth of 53% and profit growth of 49%, alongside TTM sales and profit growth of 33% and 36% [E14, E15, E16, E17]. Furthermore, the company has transformed its balance sheet into an asset of pristine strength by slashing borrowings to just ₹ 12 Cr, achieving a near-debt-free status with a debt-to-equity ratio of a mere 0.04x [E27, E28, E47]. Operational health matches this financial discipline, highlighted by debtor days improving sharply from 34.2 to 19.7 days and an impressive Sharpe ratio of 2.81 [E43, E49]. Conceded: institutional ownership has experienced negative money flow with foreign and domestic institutions reducing their stakes by a combined 6.48 percentage points [E31, E32, E33]. Nevertheless, the rules-based screen awards the company a high-confidence BUY score of 87 out of 100, vindicating its superior compounding profile [E51].

Advit Jewels trades at a steep valuation with a price-to-book ratio of 5.41x, which is nearly triple the sector benchmark of 1.94x [E2, E7]. This premium is increasingly rejected by sophisticated investors, as evidenced by a sharp reduction in foreign institutional holdings from 3.92% to 1.77% and domestic institutional holdings from 9.22% to 4.89% in just one quarter [E31, E32, E33]. The underlying quality of reported profits is also a concern, given a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.38x that suggests earnings are not being realized as cash flow [E24]. Furthermore, the business faces decelerating earnings growth and inconsistent operating margin trends, while the stock price has fallen below its 200-day moving average [E21, E23, E39, E56]. Shareholders are exposed to extreme annualised volatility of 94.6% without the benefit of any dividend yield despite the company reporting repeated profits [E4, E42, E50]. Conceded: the company has achieved high historical returns on equity [E13, E18] and has successfully reduced its debt to a negligible 0.04x equity ratio [E27, E28, E46].

The bear’s focus on a high price-to-book ratio [E2, E7] ignores that the company’s ROE of 45.6% and ROCE of 32.2% [E13, E12] are vastly superior to the sector medians of 8.9% and 10.2% [E9, E63]. While the bear claims growth is decelerating [E56], the trailing twelve-month sales and profit growth of 33% and 36% [E15, E17] are nearly double the sector medians [E61, E62], supported by a long-term operating margin expansion of 2 percentage points [E20]. Conceded: institutional holdings have declined [E31, E32, E33] and cash conversion is low [E24], but operational efficiency is clearly improving as debtor days dropped from 34.2 to 19.7 [E49]. The absence of dividends [E4, E50] is a strategic choice to fund a 150% increase in capital work-in-progress [E29], all while maintaining a nearly debt-free status [E27, E47]. Finally, despite high volatility [E42], a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E40] and a Sharpe ratio of 2.81 [E43] demonstrate that the business is delivering exceptional risk-adjusted returns.

Conceded: ROE and ROCE significantly exceed sector medians [E9, E12, E13, E63]. However, the bull's dismissal of valuation risks ignores a price-to-book ratio of 5.43x against a sector benchmark of 1.94x [E2, E7], alongside a thin margin of safety of just 4.6% [E35]. Conceded: TTM sales and profit growth outpace sector medians [E15, E17, E61, E62], yet the screening engine explicitly flags that earnings growth is decelerating [E56] and quarterly operating margins compressed by 2 percentage points year-over-year in September 2026, reading inconsistent over the last two quarters [E21, E23]. The bull's defense of zero dividends [E4, E50] as funding capital work-in-progress [E29] overlooks the severe warning that cash conversion stands at just 0.38x, meaning reported profits are far ahead of actual cash [E24]. Finally, while the bull highlights exceptional risk-adjusted returns [E40, E43], institutional money flow reads negative with a sharp 6.48 percentage point reduction in combined foreign and domestic institutional holdings [E31, E32, E33], accompanied by an annualized volatility of 94.6% [E42].
